title: An Ignatian day at home
hook: morning offering, finding God in work, examen at night

segments.voice: Yesterday, a Jesuit pope, and a retreat-house word carried into kitchens. Your line was discern. Before which small choice did you pause and ask which way draws toward love? Day one thousand two hundred seventy.

The alarm goes off. Feet on a cold floor, a kettle, a phone already buzzing, someone who can't find their shoes. No retreat house, no director, no month of silence. Just a weekday. Lately this path has walked through the Spiritual Exercises and the Jesuits who live by them. Today is the last day with them, and it asks a practical question: what does all of that look like in an ordinary house, with dishes in the sink? One Ignatian answer comes in three pieces: morning, middle and night.
screen: `AN ALARM, A KETTLE, LOST SHOES.` → `NO RETREAT HOUSE. JUST A WEEKDAY.` → `MORNING, MIDDLE, NIGHT.`

segments.voice: An Ignatian day at home. Piece one, the morning offering. Before the day runs away, a short prayer hands it to God in advance: all of it, the prayers, the work, the joys, the sufferings. One familiar version was spread by a prayer movement founded by a Jesuit, and it comes in more than one wording. It's the Suscipe in miniature: take, Lord, receive, today. Piece two, the middle of the day: God in all things. No extra hour of prayer required. The laundry, the commute, the email, the child's question become places to notice God at work, the way the young Jesuit student learned to find God over his grammar book. Contemplatives in action, at the kitchen sink. Piece three, the examen at night. Tradition says Ignatius would let a busy Jesuit shorten other prayers, but not this one. In the Exercises he lays it out simply: give thanks for the day's gifts, ask for light, go back over the hours, ask pardon where you fell short, and look toward tomorrow with hope. It takes a few minutes. It doesn't need words aloud. The psalm in the Douay-Rheims holds both ends of the day together: "To shew forth thy mercy in the morning, and thy truth in the night." Morning offering, God in all things, examen. And notice who has been with us these weeks: the Exercises, the foundation, indifference, the two standards, discernment, the Suscipe, cura personalis, the magis, the Salvadoran Jesuits, Pedro Arrupe, a Jesuit pope. All of it fits into one ordinary day. Tomorrow, a different school of prayer, on a mountain.
screen: `MORNING: HAND THE DAY OVER.` · `MIDDLE: GOD IN ALL THINGS.` · `NIGHT: THE EXAMEN.` · `THE WHOLE JESUIT WAY, IN ONE DAY.` · then, large: `THY MERCY IN THE MORNING, THY TRUTH IN THE NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: rehearse tonight's examen now, so it's ready. Settle, and breathe. Look back over the last day. First, find one thing to be grateful for, and stay with it. Second, ask for light to see the day honestly. Third, walk back through the hours, from waking until now: where did you feel close to God or to goodness, and where far away? Fourth, if something needs forgiving, say so simply. Last, look toward tomorrow. If you pray, you can do all of it in God's company. Tonight, before sleep, do it again. The bell holds the time.
An Ignatian day at home. A morning offering, God in all things through the day, and the examen at night: the Jesuit way, fitted into an ordinary house. Today's word, and the last of the Jesuits.

segments.voice: Your line: god in all things. Tonight, do the examen before you sleep, and see where the line turned up. Day one thousand two hundred seventy.

howItsDone: Catholics shaped by Ignatian spirituality begin the day with a morning offering, try to notice God through the day's work, and end it with the examen before sleep.

fork.setup: it's late, you're tired, and you've skipped prayer all day. what does the Ignatian way suggest?
options: give up: the day is lost.
do a short examen before sleep.
make up for it with an hour of prayer.
fork.reveal: Ignatius treated the examen as the prayer not to skip. a few honest minutes at night gathers up the whole day.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ignatian spirituality is for Jesuits on retreat.
what it means: a morning offering, noticing God through the day, and an examen at night, in any home.
what a scholar hears: the general examen of the Exercises, the Suscipe's offering in miniature, and Nadal's contemplatives in action.

notes: Morning offering: the best-known version is associated with the Apostleship of Prayer, founded by Jesuit François-Xavier Gautrelet; hedged in the voice ('a prayer movement founded by a Jesuit'). Confirm. The prayer is described, not quoted or written.

The examen's points are paraphrased from SpEx 43 (thanks, grace to know sins, review, pardon, amendment); the practice numbers them 'first...fourth, last' as steps of the practice, not as a claim about Ignatius's count. Confirm.
Hedged as tradition: Ignatius allowed busy Jesuits to shorten other prayer but not the examen. Confirm.
Lately in the hook refers to this path's own Jesuit section (days 1250–1270).
Douay-Rheims wording of Psalm 91:3 to confirm.
Section end: names the Jesuit section's main words and points to the Carmelites.
